# Driveline and wheel bearing noises

> **Some safety-critical values on this page are not confirmed** (marked [Unverified] or [Partial]): they come from one source or are only partly supported. Verify against the factory service manual before use; later runs re-check them against new sources.

> Items marked **[Partial]** are only partly confirmed by the source and need more work. They stay in the review queue and are firmed up, corrected or removed as more sources come in.

## Summary

[Partial] Measure driveshaft and pinion angles with a magnetic angle gauge, aiming for a one-to-three degree difference. [t373]

Load the cargo area with approximately 450 lbs and take the vehicle for a test drive. [t373]

Set the parking brake, shift into neutral, then check for up and down movement in the rear axle housing. [t126]

[Partial] Check for play up, down, side to side, noting lack of in-and-out movement suggests backlash. [t119]

[Partial] Turn off VDC, drive into sand or mud, stomp on the throttle while driving in loose terrain. [t879]

Start engine, back up with gas, drive normally to reverse, noting one pop per shift. [t1018]

[Partial] Shift transmission into neutral, apply parking brake firmly, then check rear driveshaft and slip yoke movement by twisting them. [t799]

Listen for a faint whine from the rear end while driving between 50 and 70 mph. [t794]

[Partial] Rock front wheels at 6, 12, 3, and 9 o'clock positions; drive over rough pavement or exit ramps at highway speeds while decelerating. [t495]

[Partial] Check radiator fluid for a milky appearance to inspect transmission damage. [t874]

[Partial] Remove the front differential and disconnect or remove the front driveshaft. [t345]

Listen for a whine occurring between 53mph and 59mph. [t345]

[Partial] Listen for strange popping sounds coming from the rear end while cornering. [t801]

## Procedure

> **[Partial]** Needs more work: the verifier could confirm only part of this procedure (the steps marked [Partial], or whether the list is complete). Steps or precautions may be wrong or missing; read the source thread before relying on it. Later runs fill it in as more sources are found.

1. [Partial] Start the engine with a helper watching up front.
2. Back up and apply gas to trigger a click or pop sound.
3. Shift into drive while applying throttle to hear another click or pop.
4. Drive around normally until shifting into reverse causes one final pop.

_Procedure reported by [t1018]._

1. Measure the driveshaft angle.
2. Measure the rear axle housing pinion angle.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t373] [Partial]</summary>

1. Load the cargo area with approximately 450 lbs of weight to simulate a heavier vehicle load.
2. Take the vehicle for a test drive while carrying this extra weight.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t126] [Partial]</summary>

1. Set the parking brake firmly.
2. [Partial] Shift the transmission into neutral.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t879] [Partial]</summary>

1. [Partial] Turn off the Vehicle Dynamic Control (VDC) system.
2. [Partial] Drive into sand or mud to simulate low-traction conditions.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t799] [Partial]</summary>

1. Shift the transmission into neutral.
2. Apply the parking brake firmly to hold the vehicle steady.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t794] [Partial]</summary>

1. Listen for a faint whine coming from the rear end while driving between 50 and 70 mph.
2. Observe that the noise disappears when accelerating or decelerating.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t495] [Partial]</summary>

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t874] [Partial]</summary>

1. Check the radiator fluid for a milky appearance.
2. If milky, inspect the transmission to see if it is damaged.

</details>

2. [Partial] Disconnect or remove the front driveshaft to isolate the noise source.

</details>

<details><summary>Alternate procedure [t801] [Partial]</summary>

2. [Partial] Note if a delay of about 4 seconds occurs before the differential catches up with a loud noise.

</details>

## Tools

## Specifications

- **Front diff fluid capacity**: 1.6L [t345] ([Unverified] single report)

## Tips & gotchas

- [Partial] Aim for a difference between 1 and 3 degrees between shafts to minimize vibration. [t373]
- Note that angles measured while the rear is on jackstands may differ from ground-level readings. [t373]
- [Partial] Use heavy steel plates or similar dense weights if available. [t373]
- [Partial] Aim for 450 lbs as a starting point, with room to add another 50-100 lbs if needed. [t373]
- Check for up and down movement in the rear axle housing to detect pinion play. [t126]
- Distinguish between general play and specific directional movement to diagnose backlash vs. wear. [t119]
- Stomp on the throttle while driving in loose terrain to activate the system and see it at work. [t879]
- Note that this system effectively acts as a decent alternative to a mechanical limited slip differential. [t879]
- Note that the noise happens once per gear shift and then stops repeating for a bit. [t1018]
- Check if wheels are straight before diagnosing further. [t1018]
- Check rear driveshaft movement by grabbing the shaft and rear diff yoke, twisting them in opposite directions. [t799]
- [Partial] If there is movement at the slip yoke near the transfer case, twist those components in opposite directions to check for bad u-joints. [t799]
- [Partial] Jack the vehicle up on four stands and have someone shift into drive to examine components with weight off. [t495]
- [Partial] Inspect CV boot boots for damage, as a tear can cause clicking noises when turning. [t495]
- Note that this issue often requires dealership expertise to diagnose correctly. [t874]

## Common mistakes

- [Partial] Assuming the problem is solved just because fluids look clear, as contamination can be subtle. [t874]
- [Partial] Ignoring U-joints and wheel weights before checking fluid levels. [t874]
